posts.title: Closing summary
posts.text: And, on that note, we will be closing the blog for today. Earlier, Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy has asked the leaders for another €70bn next year to fund Ukraine’s defence against Russia as he joined a key EU summit in Brussels (10:10, 13:44, 15:13, 15:26, 16:00). EU’s Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa confirmed…

Speaking at the same time, France’s Emmanuel Macron told reporters that he did not consider a diesel deal struck by Trump with Russia as useful. “This decision is not good for ‌anyone. It sends a negative signal. It a an element ⁠of division and doubt,” Macron said after an EU summit ‌in Brussels, Reuters reported.
After some concluding comments on the bloc’s response to the growing sales of Chinese electric cars in Europe, von der Leyen and Costa wrap up their press conference.

posts.text: Elsewhere, US president Donald Trump insisted that neither him nor Elon Musk was responsible for Ukraine losing Starlink access. He claimed the restrictions was not imposed by the US, and that he has a good relationship with Ukraine’s Zelenskyy, Reuters reported.

Costa gets asked if he is more confident that a deal can be found by the end of the year. And there is also a question about Marine Le Pen’s suggestions that the budget should not be decided this early given so many key elections in Europe next year that are likely to reshape the political landscape of the continent.…
Asked about Ukraine’s new financial needs, von der Leyen says that 2026 is covered, but confirms the gap for 2027 is around €70bn euros.

On migration, von der Leyen says all leaders recognise “enormous progress” made on this issue in recent years, but more needs to be done. He says the number of illegal crossings has gone down by over 56% in the last two years, and down by 34% in the first nine months of this year. Asylum applications are also falling,…

posts.text: Von der Leyen then turns to Ukraine. She says the EU’s support “matters more than ever.” She says the bloc “is doing a long, but the reality is simple: as long as this war continues, Ukraine’s financing needs will keep growing.” “Right now, the European Union and its member states account for 80% of external aid to…

Von der Leyen also mounts a defence of the commission’s proposal on the next EU budget, effectively saying that as leaders keep coming to the EU asking it to fix things, it’s understandable that it’ll need more resources. “If there’s one lesson we have painfully learned over the last seven years, that is the lesson…

Commission president von der Leyen speaks next. She points out to high energy price increases since the start of Trump’s war against Iran. “This is the reality we have to deal with today, and we discussed this intensively with the member states. Because of the fact that the member states have very different energy…

Finally, on migration, Costa says the system is “working but … must still be improved.” “Migration remains a very political issue where there are different political visions which are known to all of you. The European Council will continue to work on this issue,” he says.

posts.title: 'Ukraine remains a central priority for Europe,' EU's Costa says
posts.text: On the next EU budget, Costa says the negotiations will need to conclude by the end of the year, and there was some progress made. But with lots of diplospeak, he admits that there are still some differences between different countries, and so he needs to “accelerate” the work on this issue. On Ukraine, he says…

EU’s Costa opens the presser. He talks about good discussions on cutting red tape and competitiveness of the bloc, and confirms what Merz said earlier about a special meeting on this issue in February next year (16:43). On energy, he says that “current volatility on energy prices [is] putting intense pressure on…
“Still someone here,” von der Leyen jokes as she gets to the podium. Just about, Ursula. Just about.
